subject: Critical Thinking
title: The Ship of Theseus: Identity and Moral Responsibility Over Time
description: A 60-second lesson on The Ship of Theseus: Identity and Moral Responsibility Over Time.

hook.text: If you replace every plank of a ship, is it still the same ship?

discovery.text: If you're not the same person: should you be punished for crimes committed by your 'earlier self'?

buildup.text: The Ship of Theseus: a paradox about identity. If every component changes gradually, does the identity persist?

twist.text: Derek Parfit argued personal identity is an illusion – what matters is psychological continuity.

climax.text: This matters for ethics: criminal punishment, long-term promises, & national responsibility all assume persistent.

punchline.text: If identity changes piece by piece, responsibility may travel differently than we assume.

quiz.question: Why is the Ship of Theseus relevant to ethics?
options: It raises questions about whether we are the same person over time, affecting moral responsibility
It proves that identity doesn't exist

details.summary: The Ship of Theseus asks if an object remains the same after all its parts are replaced, raising deep questions about personal identity and whether you can be held responsible for actions by a past version of yourself.
details.whyItMatters: Identity persistence matters for criminal justice, personal responsibility, and whether promises made by a past self still bind you today.
takeaways: Gradual change challenges our concept of identity
Personal identity affects moral and legal responsibility
No consensus exists on what makes you the same person over time

faq.question: How does the Ship of Theseus relate to moral responsibility?
faq.answer: If the person who committed a crime twenty years ago has completely changed, punishment raises questions about whether the current person truly deserves it.

faq.question: What are the main philosophical solutions to the Ship of Theseus?
faq.answer: Some argue continuity of form matters, others emphasize causal connection between stages, and some deny that strict identity survives change at all.
